event_window: first trading session on or after announcement date plus the next trading session
control_order: ascending absolute offset, past before future at a tie, then control start date
calendar_assignment: global deterministic greedy assignment; no event or control trading date may be reused across distinct calendar-support blocks
own_news_interval: with date-only metadata, inclusive calendar predicate prior_trading_date <= own_announcement_date <= second_window_date; this conservatively excludes the entire prior trading date because after-close timing is unknown
main_outcome: absolute two-session event return minus mean absolute two-session control return
main_model: event fixed effects plus x_std, same_sic2, x_std:in_same_sic2, log_size and log_liquidity
weights: each issuer-event has total weight one; rows are equal-weighted within issuer-event

exposed_h1_benchmark.status: development comparison only; H1 was row-weighted and did not estimate the direct pooled interaction, so this is not an identical estimand

multiplicity: two primary quantities use Bonferroni-adjusted two-sided 97.5% marginal intervals, giving 95% familywise coverage conditional on the cluster-sandwich approximation

scientific_decision_rule.continue_mechanism_feasibility: both familywise interval lower bounds exceed zero and both estimates remain positive in every leave-one-calendar-block and leave-one-issuer deletion
scientific_decision_rule.stop_signal_route: with the support gate passed, either familywise interval upper bound is at or below zero
scientific_decision_rule.inconclusive_stop_spending: all other outcome patterns; non-significance is not zero and no economic threshold is invented

support_gate.interpretation: study-specific triage for a finite descriptive interval, not a general validity or power guarantee

inference: calendar-support-block cluster sandwich with finite-sample factor and t reference on G-1 degrees of freedom; descriptive under explicit cross-block independence assumption
